instruction: Navigate to slide 5 and make the subtitle text bold.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to slide 5, selected 2 shapes, opened Format > Character > Font Effects, set font color to #FFFF00 via custom color picker, but the color change did not properly apply to all text runs.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between slides in LibreOffice Impress, select objects with Ctrl+A, open Format > Character dialog, navigate Font Effects tab, use custom color picker with hex values, save files with Ctrl+S
metadata.failure_analysis: Model selected shapes and applied color via Character dialog, but the font color change did not persist. The Character dialog workflow was demonstrated successfully, so a different formatting property (bold) may succeed.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different formatting property (bold) using the same Character dialog workflow the model demonstrated. The subtitle text on slide 5 is currently not bold, so applying bold is a clear, verifiable change. Bold can also be applied via Ctrl+B shortcut, offering an easier path.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to slide 5 and making the subtitle text ('Include a credit, citation, or supporting message') bold. Getter extracts bold status of text runs in slide 5 shape 4. Metric checks all runs are bold with partial credit.

scoring_breakdown.bold: 1.0 - All text runs in subtitle shape are bold (partial credit per run)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads slide 5 (index 4, 0-based) from the pptx file and extracts bold status of all text runs in the specified shape.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('expected_bold', True) without incorrect nesting.
Partial credit scoring is appropriate: returns ratio of bold runs to total runs.
Postconfig correctly saves the file with Ctrl+S before getter reads it, ensuring state freshness.
Getter properly handles edge cases: file not found, slide/shape out of range, shape without text frame.
bool(run.font.bold) correctly treats None (inherited/not-set) as False, which is semantically correct.

Minor concern: shape_index=4 is hardcoded and assumes this is the subtitle shape. Typical PPTX layouts have subtitle at lower indices, but the task metadata explicitly identifies shape 4 as the subtitle for this specific file.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a shape name or placeholder type check (e.g., checking for PP_PLACEHOLDER.SUBTITLE) instead of relying on a hardcoded shape_index, to make the getter more robust against layout variations.
